senses.gloss:
बंह् बंह्, also written वंह् (related to
2. बृह्), cl. 1. A. बंहते, बबंहे, बं-
हिता, &c., to grow, increase: Caus. P. बंहयति,
यितुम्, to cause to grow, increase, strengthen, fix,
make firm; [cf. बहल, बहु, बहुल.]
बंहिमन्, आ, m. muchness, abundance, multitude.

बंहिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (superl. of बहुल), very
much, very many, most abundant, very abundant,
very great, excessive.

बंहीयस्, आन्, असी, अस् (compar. of बहुल), much
more, more abundant, very many, exceeding.
बन्द् बन्द्. See rt. बद्, p. 671, col. 3.
बन्दि बन्दि, बन्दिन्, &c. See वन्दि, &c.

बन्दिआरयु बन्दिआरयु, N. of a place men-
tioned in the Romaka-siddhānta.

बन्ध् बन्ध् [cf. rt. बुन्ध्], cl. 9. P. (ep.
also A.) बध्नाति (बध्नीते), Impv. 2nd
sing. बधान, बबन्ध (Ved. 3rd pl. बेधुस्,
2nd sing. A. बेधिषे), भन्त्स्यति (ep. also बन्-
धिष्यति, -ते), अभान्त्सीत्, बन्द्धुम् (ep. also बन्-
धितुम्), to bind, tie, fix, fasten; to chain, enchain,
fetter; to fasten or tie round, bind round, put on (e. g.
चीरम् बध्नन्ति मुनयः, the ascetics put on
clothing made of strips of bark); (A.) to bind on
one's self, put on; to ensnare; to catch (e. g. मत्-
स्यान् बन्ध्, to catch fish), take captive, take
prisoner; to shut up, confine, imprison; to inflict
punishment, punish, chastise; to bind a sacrificial
victim, offer, sacrifice (with dat. of the deity to whom
the victim is presented, Ved.); to fix, direct, fasten
(the eyes or mind) upon (with loc.); to shut, close,
stop, stop up, preclude; to arrest, hold back, check,
suppress; to overpower, oppress, violate; to bind
together, put together, fasten together, join, com-
bine, connect, conglomerate, unite; to construct,
build; to construct verses, compose; to bring to pass,
effect, produce, evoke, result in, be followed by
(with acc.); to form fruit (as a plant), to set; to
strike (root); to take up (an abode); to manifest,
exhibit, evince, display, show (e. g. धृतिम् ब-
धान, show thy resolution); to entertain, cherish,
foster, possess, have, contract, form; अञ्जलिम् बन्ध्,
to place the two hands hollowed side by side;
मुष्टिम् बन्ध्, to clench the fist; सेतुम् बन्ध्,
to construct a dam, build a bridge, (बन्धिष्ये
सेतुना गङ्गाम्, I will span the Gaṅgā with a
bridge); गोलम् बन्ध्, to form or construct a
globe; भ्रु-कुटिम् बन्ध्, to knit the brows,
frown; सौहृद्यम् or सख्यम् or अजर्यम् बन्ध्
to contract friendship; वैरम् बन्ध्, to contract
enmity: Pass. बध्यते, Aor. अबधि (?), to be
bound; to bind on one's self, put on: Caus. बन्-
धयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अबबन्धत्, to cause to
bind, cause to be bound; to order to be imprisoned;
to cause to be joined together or constructed, cause
to be built, cause to be embanked; (according to
the Dhātu-pāṭha) to bind, (in this last sense also
बाधयति): Desid. बिभत्सति, to wish to bind:
Intens. बाबध्यते, बाबन्द्धि, to bind fast, tie
firmly; [cf. Zend band, banda, baś-ta, ‘bound;’ Gr.
πείθω, πεῖσ-μα for πενθ-μα, πενθερός; Lat. pat-
ibulum, pendo, pendeo, fī-lum for fid-lum, fū-
nis for fud-nis, fīd-es, fīd-o for feido = πείθω,
fœd-us; Slav. vjazati, ‘to bind;’ Goth. bind-an,
fastan; Old Germ. fasti; Angl. Sax. bindan,
bonda, bœnd, bœst, fœst; Iceland. fas-t.]

बन्ध, अस्, m. binding, tying, a bond, tie, chain,
fetter, knot, halter, tether [cf. पाद-ब्˚]; a ligature,
bandage; laying snares; catching, capturing, capture;
binding in fetters, fettering, confining, imprisoning,
confinement, imprisonment, custody [cf. राज-ब्˚];
fixing, directing (the mind towards anything); bind-
ing together, joining, uniting [cf. पाणि-ब्˚]; joining
the hollowed hands; forming, constructing, construc-
tion, building, erecting (e. g. सेतोर् बन्धः, the
construction of an embankment or bridge; cf. सेतु-
ब्˚); embanking, an embankment, throwing a bridge
across (a river); contracting or knitting the brows
[cf. भ्रुकुटि-ब्˚]; joining the hands or feet in
particular positions, any posture or position of the
limbs or body generally, a position, posture (e. g.
आसन-ब्˚, a sitting posture); a particular position of
[]
the hands and feet [cf. महा-ब्˚, मूल-ब्˚]; a par-
ticular position in coitus; connection, intercourse,
society; agreement, union; manifestation, exhibition,
display [cf. राग-ब्˚]; consequence, result (e. g.
अरिष्ट-ब्˚, having welfare as a consequence, causing
welfare); a sinew, tendon; a pledge, deposit, (per-
haps rather) pledging [cf. बन्धक]; that with
which anything is bound together or bordered,
border, framework, inclosure; (in philosophy) bon-
dage, (opposed to मुक्ति, मोक्ष, and regarded in
the Sāṅkhya system as threefold, viz. प्रकृति-ब्˚,
वैकारिक-ब्˚, दक्षिणा-ब्˚; cf. कर्म-ब्˚, दक्-
षिणा-ब्˚); (in rhetoric) combination of sounds, con-
struction of words; a disease in which the eyelids
cannot be wholly closed; (in comp. with numerals)
a part [cf. दश-ब्˚, पञ्च-ब्˚; cf. also Lat. pondus;
Lith. bandà, ‘a herd of cattle;’ Angl. Sax. bonda,
bœnd, bœst; Hib. bad = Armor. bód, ‘a bunch,
bush, cluster, tuft, thicket.’]
—बन्ध-करण, अम्,
n. binding, fettering, restraining, holding back,
preventing, impeding.
—बन्ध-कर्तृ, ता, त्री,
तृ, a binder, one who fetters or restrains.
—बन्-
ध-तन्त्र, अम्, n. a complete army, or one pos-
sessing the four divisions of chariots, elephants, horse,
and foot.
—बन्ध-देश, N. of a country men-
tioned in the Ratna-koṣa.
—बन्ध-पारुष्य,
अम्, n. forced construction of words.
—बन्ध-
मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of bonds or ties, serving
for a bond, being of the nature of a bond.
—बन्-
ध-मुद्रा, f. the impression or mark of fetters.
—बन्ध-मोचनिका or बन्ध-मोचिनी, f. ‘re-
leasing from bonds,’ N. of a Yoginī.
—बन्ध-
स्तम्भ, अस्, m. ‘binding-post,’ the post to which
an elephant is tied.

बन्धक, अस्, m. a binder, one who is employed
in binding; one who catches, a catcher [cf. नाग-ब्˚];
a violator, ravisher; a band, tie [cf. पशु-ब्˚]; a bank,
dam, dike [cf. जल-ब्˚]; any posture of the body
[cf. मल्ल-ब्˚]; a pledge, deposit, pawn, (perhaps
rather) pledging; a promise, vow (= सत्यङ्-कार);
exchanging, barter; (in comp. with numerals, espe-
cially at the end of an adj. comp.) a part, portion
(e. g. ऋणं स-दश-बन्धकम्, a debt plus one
tenth); a city; (अम्), n. binding, confinement; (ई),
f. an unchaste woman (‘connected with many men;’
कुमार-बन्धकी, a woman unchaste even as a
girl); a harlot, courtezan, wanton [cf. बन्धुकी];
a barren woman [cf. बन्ध्या]; a female elephant.
—बन्धक-त्व, अम्, n. the being fettered.

बन्धन, अस्, ई, अम्, binding, tying, fettering
[cf. भाव-ब्˚]; holding fast, arresting, checking,
stopping; (at the end of a comp.) dependant on,
depending upon; (अम्), n. the act of binding, tying,
fastening, fettering; a bond, chain, fetter; a tether,
halter; a sinew, muscle [cf. श्लथ-ब्˚]; binding on,
binding round; binding up; a ligature, bandage;
joining, connection; catching, capturing; confining,
confinement, captivity, bondage, detention, im-
prisonment; a gaol, prison; inflicting pain, hurting;
putting to death; joining, connecting, uniting;
forming, building, constructing, construction; सेतोर्
बन्धनम्, the construction of an embankment
or bridge [cf. सेतु-बन्ध, सेतु-बन्धन]; a
bar, barrier; embanking, an embankment, bridging
over; mixing, alloying, alloyage (of metals); con-
junction, connection, coherence; a stalk, stem, pe-
duncle [cf. प्रसव-ब्˚]; गीत-बन्धन, a com-
position which is sung, an epic poem rehearsed in
singing; (अम्, ई), n. f. any instrument of binding or
holding together, a bond (e. g. अन्नम् प्राणस्य
बन्धनम्, food is the bond, i. e. the staff of
life), band, rope, tie, cord, string, garter, thread;
a tether, halter [cf. पाद-ब्˚]; a chain, fetter; a
snare; a ligature, bandage.
—बन्धन-ग्रन्थि,
इस्, m. the knot of a ligature; a noose; a rope for
tying cattle.
—बन्धन-पालक, अस्, m. a gaol-
keeper, gaoler, turnkey.
—बन्धन-रज्जु, उस्,
f. a rope for tying cattle; any rope or string used
for tying.
—बन्धन-वेश्मन्, अ, n. ‘house of
bondage,’ a prison.
—बन्धन-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्,
being in prison, living in confinement, imprisoned,
[]
captive; (अस्), m. a prisoner, captive.
—बन्धन-
स्थान, अम्, n. (a place where cattle are fastened),
a stall, stable.
—बन्धनागार (˚न-अग्˚ or -आग्˚),
अस्, अम्, m. n. ‘house of bondage,’ a prison.
—बन्-
धनाधिकार (˚न-अध्˚), अस्, m., N. of the third
chapter of the first part of the Rasendra-kalpa-druma,
a medical work by Rāma-kṛṣṇa.
—बन्धनालय
(˚न-आल्˚), अम्, n. ‘house of bondage,’ a prison.

बन्धनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be bound or tied, to
be bound on, to be bound round; anything bound
on or tied round; to be confined, to be captured or
taken prisoner; to be embanked; (अस्), m. (accord-
ing to a Scholiast) = सेतु, an embankment.

बन्धयितृ, ता, m. one who binds or ties up,
a binder.

बन्धित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused to be bound (e. g.
शतम् बन्धितः, caused to be bound for a hundred
pieces of money, i. e. imprisoned for a debt of a
hundred pieces of money); bound.

बन्धित्र, अम्, n. (?), the god of love, love,
desire [cf. वधित्र]; a spot, mole.

बन्धिन्, ई, इनी, इ, (at the end of a comp.) binding
[cf. दृढ-बन्धिनी]; catching [cf. मत्स्य-ब्˚];
causing, effecting, producing, exciting, evoking [cf.
फल-ब्˚, राग-ब्˚]; showing, exhibiting, manifest-
ing, evincing [cf. वात्सल्य-ब्˚].

बन्धु, उस्, m. connection, conjunction, relation-
ship, association; relation, reference, respect (e. g.
केन बन्धुना, in what respect ?); one who is
connected with or belongs to (any profession or tribe,
especially if only nominally so connected; cf. क्ष-
त्र-ब्˚, द्विज-ब्˚, ब्रह्म-ब्˚); a kinsman, relation,
relative, connection, kindred in general [cf. मातृ-ब्˚];
(in law) a cognate kinsman in a remote degree, one
subsequent in right of inheritance to the Sa-gotra,
(three kinds of these are enumerated, personal, pater-
nal, and maternal: the first are sons of the deceased
father's sister, of his mother's sister, and of his ma-
ternal uncle: the second are the sons of his father's
paternal aunt, of his father's maternal aunt, and of
his father's maternal uncle: the third are the sons
of his mother's paternal aunt, of his mother's ma-
ternal aunt, and of his mother's maternal uncle); a
friend [cf. अ-ब्˚, अमृत-ब्˚, ऋषि-ब्˚]; a husband;
a brother; N. of a flower (= बन्धूक); N. of a
metre; (in astron.) N. of the fourth mansion; N.
of a Ṛṣi with the patronymic Gaupāyana or Lau-
pāyana, author of two hymns in the Ṛg-veda; (ac-
cording to Yāska also) wealth; according to Pāṇini
a feminine word ending in या must change या to ई
before बन्धु in a comp., e. g. कारीष-गन्ध्या-
बन्धु becomes कारीष-गन्धी-बन्धु; [cf.
Hib. badh, ‘love, friendship.’]
—बन्धु-काम, अस्,
आ, अम्, loving relations, affectionate towards relations
and friends.
—बन्धु-कृत्य, अम्, n. the duty of a
kinsman or of a friend, a friendly office, friendly service.
—बन्धु-क्षित्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. dwelling among rela-
tions; (Sāy.) having the quality or condition of kin-
dred; (according to some this word may be the N.
of a person or family.)
—बन्धु-जन, अस्, m. a
kinsman, relation, friend; kinsfolk, relations.
—बन्-
धु-जीव or बन्धु-जीवक, अस्, m. ‘living in associ-
ation or groups,’ Pentapetes Phœnicea, (a plant with a
red flower which opens at midday and withers away
the next morning at sunrise); (अम्), n. its flower;
(कस्), m., N. of a Cakra-vartin.
—बन्धुजीव-
पुष्प, अम्, n. the flower of Pentapetes Phœnicea.
—बन्धुजीवाभि-ताम्र (˚व-अभ्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
deep red like the blossom of Pentapetes Phœnicea.
—बन्धु-ता, f. relations collectively, kindred, kin
(= बन्धूनां समूहः); relationship, affinity,
connection, relation.
—बन्धु-त्व, अम्, n. relation-
ship, brotherhood, affinity.
—बन्धु-दग्ध, अस्,
आ, अम्, ‘destroyed or consumed by relations,’ i. e. an
abandoned wretch (= हतक).
—बन्धु-दत्त, अस्,
आ, अम्, given by relations or by a kinsman; (अस्), m.,
N. of a man; (आ), f., N. of a woman; (अम्), n. a
particular kind of female property (given to a girl
by her relations at her marriage).
—बन्धु-दायाद,
अस्, m. a kinsman and heir.
—बन्धु-पति, इस्, m.
lord of kindred or relations; [cf. बान्धुपत.]
[]
—बन्धु-पाल, अस्, m. ‘kindred-protector,’ N. of
a man.
—बन्धु-पालित, अस्, m. ‘kindred-pro-
tected,’ N. of a prince.
—बन्धु-पुष्प-माल, अस्,
आ, अम्, wearing a chaplet of Bandhu flowers.
—बन्-
धु-पृछ्, ट्, m., Ved. asking relations, inquiring after
kindred, (Sāy. = बन्धूनाम् प्रष्टा); [cf. पृष्-
ट-बन्धु.]
—बन्धु-प्रभ, अस्, m., N. of a
Vidyā-dhara.
—बन्धु-प्रीति, इस्, f. affection for a
friend, love of relatives or friends.
—बन्धु-भाव,
अस्, m. friendship.
—बन्धु-भाषित, अम्, n. the
talk or speech of kindred.
—बन्धु-मत्, आन्, अती,
अत्, having relations, surrounded by relations; (आन्),
m., N. of a man; of a king; (अती), f., N. of two
women; N. of a town.
—बन्धु-वञ्चक, अस्, m.
‘deceiver of relatives,’ N. of a Vidūṣaka.
—बन्धु-
वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having relations or kindred.
—बन्-
धु-वर्ग, अस्, m. the whole body of relations, circle
of kinsmen, kindred.
—बन्धु-हीन, अस्, आ, अम्,
destitute of kindred, relationless, friendless.
—बन्-
धू-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्तुम्, to make a friend
of.
—बन्धू-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made a friend.
—बन्ध्व्-एष, अस्, m., Ved. inquiring after kin-
dred, (Sāy. = बन्धूनाम् अन्वेषणम्.)

बन्धूक, अस्, m. a shrub bearing a red flower,
Pentapetes Phœnicea [cf. बन्धु-जीव]; Terminalia
Tomentosa; (अम्), n. the flower of Pentapetes Phœ-
nicea.
—बन्धूक-पुष्प, अस्, m. the tree Termi-
nalia Tomentosa.
—बन्धूकपुष्प-रजस्, अस्, n.
the pollen of the above flower.

बान्धुक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. बन्धुक), belonging
to or derived from the Bandhuka tree.

बन्धुकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, coming from or belonging
to an unchaste woman.

बन्धुदा, f. an unchaste woman; (perhaps
wrongly for बन्धुरा.)

बन्धुर, अस्, आ, अम्, uneven, undulating, fluc-
tuating, wavy; bowed, bent, inclined, depressed,
crooked; pleasing, delightful, handsome, beautiful;
deaf; injurious, mischievous; (अस्), m. a goose; a
crane; a drug (= विडङ्ग ऋषभ); a plant (=
बन्धूक); oil-cake; the vulva; (आ), f. a prostitute;
(आस्), f. pl. the meal of parched corn; (अम्), n. a
diadem, crest; [cf. Angl. Sax. bendan.]

बन्धूर, अस्, आ, अम्, wavy, undulating, uneven;
bowing, bent; beautiful; (अस्), m. a hole, a chasm.
बन्धुरित, अस्, आ, अम्, bent, inclined, depressed.
बन्धूलि, इस्, m. a plant (= बन्धूक).

बन्ध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be bound or fettered,
to be confined or imprisoned; to be bound together,
to be joined; to be constructed; detained, confined,
under arrest; stopped; not bearing fruit in due
season, barren, unfruitful, unproductive, fruitless, idle,
useless, unprofitable, vain; not having the menstrual
courses; destitute, deprived of (with inst. or at the
end of a comp., e. g. प्रजा-ब्˚, destitute of offspring);
(आ), f. a barren or childless woman; a barren cow;
a kind of perfume commonly called Bāla.
—बन्-
ध्य-ता, f. or बन्ध्य-त्व, अम्, n. barrenness,
sterility, uselessness; want, deficiency, scarcity, desti-
tution.
—बन्ध्य-पर्वत, N. of a district.
—बन्-
ध्य-फल, अस्, आ, अम्, fruitless, useless, idle, vain.
—बन्ध्यफल-ता, f. fruitlessness, uselessness.
—बन्ध्या-कर्कोटकी, f. a species of medicinal
plant given to barren women; [cf. पुत्र-दा.]
—बन्ध्या-तनय, अस्, m. = बन्ध्या-पुत्र,
q. v.
—बन्ध्या-त्व, अम्, n. sterility, barrenness.
—बन्ध्या-दुहितृ, ता, f. the daughter of a barren
woman, a mere chimæra or anything merely ima-
ginary which does not really exist.
—बन्ध्या-
पुत्र, अस्, m. the son of a barren woman, i. e. any-
thing merely imaginary, an impossibility; [cf. ग-
गण-पुष्प.]
—बन्ध्या-रोग, अस्, m., N. of a
chapter of the Prayogāmṛta, a medical work by
Vaidya-cintāmaṇi.
—बन्ध्या-सुत, अस्, or बन्-
ध्या-सूनु, उस्, m. = बन्ध्या-पुत्र, q. v.

बन्ध्यायमान, अस्, आ, अम्, becoming barren
or useless.

बन्ध्र or बन्द्ध्र, अम्, n. a band, tie,
(in अ-ब्˚, q. v.)

बान्धकिनेय बान्धकिनेय, अस्, m. (fr. बन्-
धकी), the son of an unmarried woman, a bastard.

बान्धव बान्धव, अस्, m. (fr. बन्धु), a
relation (near or remote and including wives and chil-
dren), relative, kinsman [cf. पितृ-ब्˚]; a maternal
relation; a friend [cf. पिक-ब्˚]; (ई), f. a female rela-
tion.
